title: Beef, Loin, Tenderloin Roast, Separable Lean Only, Boneless, Trimmed to 0" Fat, Select, Cooked, Roasted

content.title: About
content.content: Beef tenderloin is one of the most tender cuts, located along the spine. This product is the separable lean portion, boneless, trimmed to 0" fat, select grade, and cooked by roasting. It offers a buttery texture, mild flavor, and high protein content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tenderloin is the leanest and most expensive beef cut.
Roasting at high heat locks in flavor while preserving nutrients.
In the USDA database, code 5608 refers to cooked, roasted, lean-only tenderloin.
It is a staple in fine‑dining dishes such as filet mignon.
A proper sear creates a flavorful crust while keeping the interior pink.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 22 g of complete protein, essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Very low fat content
items.content: Trimmed to 0" fat, it contains less than 2 g of fat per 100 g, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in iron and zinc
items.content: Provides heme iron and zinc, supporting immune function and blood health.

items.title: B‑vitamin complex
items.content: Contains B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: The combination of protein and micronutrients helps maintain and build lean muscle.

items.title: Possible bacterial contamination
items.content: If not stored properly, cooked beef can harbor Salmonella or E. coli.

items.title: Added sodium in processed versions
items.content: Pre‑seasoned roasted products may contain extra salt; people with hypertension should watch portions.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef proteins.

items.title: Digestive heaviness
items.content: Large servings can feel heavy due to the dense protein content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the roasted tenderloin hot, sliced thinly. It pairs well with roasted vegetables, mashed potatoes, red‑wine or mushroom sauces. It can also be added to salads, sandwiches, or diced for stir‑fries.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked product refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight container at –18 °C for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C before eating.
